name: Can an estimate be done before architectural plans are finished?

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to get a useful construction estimate before final permit plans are ready?
mainEntity.text: Is it possible to get a useful construction estimate before final permit plans are ready?

acceptedAnswer.text: A preliminary estimate can absolutely be done before final plans are complete, and in many cases it is the smartest time to start budgeting. Estimators can work from concept sketches, a program list, early floor plans, or a scope narrative. The estimate should be clearly labeled as preliminary and should include assumptions about size, finish level, structural complexity, site conditions, and permit requirements. That is especially useful in Los Angeles, where design changes can have a big impact on budget. The key is to avoid treating a conceptual estimate like a fixed price. It is a planning tool that helps the owner decide whether the project is feasible and where to adjust scope before investing in full drawings and engineering. Once the design is further along, the estimate should be updated and tightened so the budget reflects the actual project scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a useful preliminary estimate can be created from concept drawings, a scope outline, or a feasibility study. It will be less precise than a final bid and should include assumptions, allowances, and contingency because design details are still missing.
